realism.reason: Faces and skin are convincing, and the lighting reads as airport. Three AI tells remain. The departure board shows pseudo-text like 'AIRO', 'CAUSES' and garbled city names. The aircraft carries a garbled livery ('SQ SANTEILE') and a nonsense tail logo. A small glowing teal capsule floats on her hair part in shot 2.

visual_consistency.reason: Her face, hair and camel coat with white tee hold across shots 1–3. Her outer layer changes from a hip-length blazer (shots 1–2) to a long overcoat (shot 3). In shot 4 she is small and mid-sip, so her face can't be verified as a match and the 'calm confident smile' payoff is lost.

brief_adherence.reason: The story beats are followed: disruption, phone moment, walk-away, lounge, end card. Several specs are missed. The board was meant to have no legible characters. Shot 2 has a floating graphic artifact despite the 'no floating graphics' rule. The shot 4 overlay sits in the lower-left over the chair and near her body instead of the clean upper third. The on-screen copy deviates: 'Already covered.' is replaced by the notification, and 'Delays. Cancellations. Covered.' becomes a checklist. That copy works but is off-brief.

hook_strength.reason: A tight, red-lit face with a CANCELLED stamp and 'NOW WHAT?' is instantly relatable and readable with sound off. It is strong scroll-stopping tension in the first second.

advertising_quality.reason: The narrative and motion graphics are clean and premium. The notification card, checklist and end card are well designed and legible, and the brand promise lands without sound. Garbled airline text in the hero resolution shot and the hair artifact undercut the trust the brand is selling, and the hero shot lacks a readable emotional payoff.

issues: Garbled pseudo-text on the departure board in the hook (header and row names partially legible)
Small glowing teal capsule artifact on her hair part in shot 2
Garbled airline livery 'SQ SANTEILE' and nonsense tail logo on the aircraft in shot 4
Wardrobe drift: hip-length blazer in shots 1–2 becomes a long overcoat in shot 3
Shot 4: her face is hidden by the cup and she is small in frame, so there is no visible calm smile and identity can't be confirmed
Shot 4 overlay placed lower-left over the chair and near her legs instead of the upper third as specified
Eyes-closed smile while walking toward camera in shot 3 reads slightly odd/staged
creative.regeneration_notes: Shot 1: render the departure board as an abstract field of glowing red horizontal bars with no glyphs or characters at all, using heavy defocus (f/1.4) so there is no readable text, headers or logos. Shot 2: add 'no glowing objects, no lights or graphics on hair or body' and keep the phone screen fully facing away from camera. Shot 3: lock wardrobe to 'hip-length camel blazer, white crew tee, dark jeans' in every shot, matching shots 1–2. Use 'eyes open, soft relaxed smile, looking slightly past camera.' Shot 4: use a plain white aircraft with no livery, no text, no logos and a blank tail. Frame a medium shot so she is larger in frame, and capture the moment she lowers the cup to show a clear calm smile with her face unobstructed. Keep the upper third of frame as clean sky for the overlay and move the checklist into that upper third in the edit. Match skin texture and warm key light to shot 3.
